Subject: Non-dilutive starter sweetener + demo credits — terms & ops

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Cedar Labs is excited about the latency/cost profile you showed. A few program questions from our side as we finalize the cohort offer:

- We run a 10-company winter accelerator and would like to offer each company a non-dilutive starter allocation for onboarding (looking at $2,000 in hosted credits per company).
- We also want a short demo credit (sandbox) to be redeemable toward a Dedicated conversion within 90 days — ideally with a conversion credit (e.g., apply unused starter credits to first-month Dedicated invoice).

Operational asks: what paperwork do you need (PO, addendum, MOU)? Any accounting or billing constraints we should flag? Also: can Redwood provide a simple term sheet we can share with sponsors and cohort companies?

Attached: Cedar_Onboarding_Scope.pdf (PDF, 145KB)

Appreciate a quick outline of options and any limitations on promo stacking or conversion windows. Hoping to publish the program offer by next Monday.

Best,
Emily Wong
Program Manager, Cedar Labs
emily@cedarlabs.com

From: evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Non-dilutive starter sweetener + demo credits — terms & ops

Hi Emily — great to connect. Love the cohort concept; we can accommodate but want to be explicit about the mechanics so expectations are clear. High-level options (pick one or we can mix):

1) Pilot Grant (no upfront invoice): 10 x $2,000 hosted credits (valid 12 months). No stacking with other Redwood promos.

2) Pilot + Conversion Credit: 10 x $2,000 hosted credits + up to 50% of remaining starter credits applied to first-month Dedicated invoice if company signs Dedicated within 90 days. Conversion requires signed Dedicated contract and minimum 3-month commit.

3) Sponsored co-fund (Cedar pays a portion, Redwood discounts): sponsor invoices Cedar; Redwood applies sponsor discount to accounts.

Operational notes: we need either a PO or an MOU signed by Cedar to enable account creation at scale. If you prefer the Pilot Grant route, we can issue grant codes for each startup and a consolidated report. For the Conversion Credit route, we’ll need the legal entity names and billing contacts for any company that converts so finance can apply credit to the first invoice.

I attached a draft term sheet with the standard onramp language and a suggested token cap per company. If you like option 2 I’ll push for a 20% first-year discount on Dedicated as part of the conversion sweetener, but that needs internal finance sign-off.

Attached: REDFW-Onramp-Terms-draft.pdf (PDF, 220KB)

Would you be available for a short 30-min call Thursday to align on which option?

Best,
Evelyn Hart

Subject: internal: Cedar Labs pilot — suggested commercial carveout and impact

Evelyn / Lauren —

Following Emily's ask, I ran a quick estimate. Proposed commercial carveout to approve:

- Offer: 10 starter grants @ $2,000 each = $20k total notional.
- Conversion sweetener: allow up to 50% of unused starter credits to apply to first-month Dedicated invoice if the company signs within 90 days (requires 3-month min commit on Dedicated).
- Max exposure cap: $24k (includes potential overage buffer + GAAP hedging).
- Per-company guardrails: 1M token cap / month while on starter credits; excess billed at standard hosted rate.

Estimated P&L / ARR impact: if 3/10 convert to Dedicated at our proposed 20% first-year discount, expected 12-month net ARR of ~$48k across conversions vs. baseline. Worst-case cash realization: $0 in revenue if none convert; cost equals utilized hosting tokens (~$3k–$8k depending on usage).

Attached: usage_estimate_Q4.csv

Ask: Lauren — finance sign-off on the exposure cap and ability to bill-consolidate for applied credits. Marcus — confirm discount approval authority (20% first-year). If we get both, I recommend option 2 (Pilot + Conversion Credit).

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager, Partnerships
ben_carter@redwood.com

Ben / Evelyn —

Finance can provisionally approve the exposure cap of $24k and the token-guardrails you proposed. Conditions:

- We require a signed MOU or PO from Cedar Labs that references the Cedar cohort program and the Redwood onramp terms. PO should include Cedar's billing entity and remit-to details.
- For any applied conversion credits, Redwood requires the converting startup's legal entity name, billing address, and VAT/tax info prior to invoice issuance.
- All starter grants will be tracked centrally; Cedar must accept our standard grant terms (we'll attach a one-page addendum).

Operationally we can centralize invoicing to Cedar (sponsor pays) or invoice individual startups. If Cedar will be the sponsor, we also need their W-9 / tax docs for US tax processing.

I'll review the final term sheet and share redlines by EOD Wednesday.
